summary: Client singleton of mod.io dependency requests in flight, used by ls::ugc::ModDependencyCachedRequestSystem (macOS Update and SendRequests(HashSet<ModItemDependenciesInfoID> const&, HashMap<ls::Guid, ModItemDependenciesInfoID>&)): SendRequests asks the UGC service for each id and stores request Guid -> id. The component holds two maps of that same type (same Windows destructor for both halves). Live: idle, all zero.

fields.name: ModId
fields.evidence: ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoID: Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540 compares ids as '(*a == *b) && ((char)a[1] == (char)b[1])' (a qword and the byte at +8) and hashes them as '*id % bucket count'; keys/elements have a 16-byte stride. macOS ModDependencyCachedRequestSystemHelper::RequestItemDependencies(unsigned long long, bool): the 64-bit mod item id.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: The byte compared at +8 (Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540): the bool argument of RequestItemDependencies(unsigned long long, bool) on macOS; meaning not established.

fields.name: Requests
fields.evidence: ls::HashMap<ls::Guid, ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoID> (macOS SendRequests parameter type). Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4ED0 (gets this singleton through bg3.exe+0x3BE40D0) hashes keys as '(guid.lo ^ guid.hi) % buckets' (the Guid hash), removes answered request Guids and inserts new ones with 16-byte values ('*v = id.lo; v[1] = id.hi', value storage +0x30, key count +0x2C); EVERY sent request goes here. Creator bg3.exe+0x3BE5960 zeroes two map patterns; destructor bg3.exe+0x682800 frees trivial values and the plain-key set.

fields.name: field_40
fields.evidence: Same map type at +0x40 (buckets +0x48, values +0x70, count +0x6C): bg3.exe+0x3BE4ED0 inserts into it only the requests of its second input list (written into both maps), and removes answered Guids from both; the per-frame update bg3.exe+0x3BE3780 walks its values (16-byte stride, qword = mod id). Which request kind the second list is was not established - so the name stays unknown.

open_questions: What distinguishes the requests that also go into the +0x40 map (the second list built by bg3.exe+0x3BE4270) - the +0x40 map keeps an unknown name.
second_pass: Both maps settled on Windows from bg3.exe+0x3BE4ED0: Guid keys (Guid hash), 16-byte ModItemDependenciesInfoID values (qword + bool, compared in bg3.exe+0x3BE4540), the second map a subset of the first.
